topic.angle: Swift (2004) sinking after the 2024 solar max; $30M Katalyst LINK built in <1 year; Pegasus XL from Stargazer L-1011 at ~40,000 ft over Kwajalein July 3 2026; attitude-control failure; no capture (Aug 19); came within 7.5-9 mi; Swift shut down Oct 20 at 171 mi, re-entered Nov 4 2026 over Indonesia.
topic.title: NASA Sent a Robot to Save a Falling Telescope. It Never Touched It.

versions.description:
NASA paid $30 million for a robot to save its falling Swift telescope. The LINK spacecraft launched from under a jet, got within 7.5 to 9 miles of Swift, and never touched it. Here is how the rescue was built in less than a year, and why it failed.

In this episode:
0:00 The robot that never touched Swift
0:13 Swift: 20+ years catching gamma-ray bursts
0:24 Why Swift started falling
0:45 A $30 million rescue robot in under a year
1:22 Launched from under a jet
1:46 What went wrong
2:12 The end of Swift

Sources:
- NASA, Swift Boost Mission: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/swift/swift-boost-mission/
- NASA, Swift Boost Mission timeline: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/swift/swift-boost-mission/timeline/
- NASA, "NASA Highlights Lessons Learned From Swift Boost Mission": https://science.nasa.gov/missions/swift/nasa-highlights-lessons-learned-from-swift-boost-mission/
- NASA, "Commercial Spacecraft for NASA's Swift Boost Continues Tech Demo" (Sept 4, 2026): https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/swift/2026/09/04/commercial-spacecraft-for-nasas-swift-boost-continues-tech-demo/
- NASA, "NASA's Swift Mission Ends Ahead of Re-Entry" (Oct 23, 2026): https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/swift/2026/10/23/nasas-swift-mission-ends-ahead-of-re-entry/
- NASA, "NASA's Swift Observatory to Re-enter Atmosphere" (updated Nov 4, 2026): https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/swift/2026/11/02/nasas-swift-observatory-to-re-enter-atmosphere/
- NASA, contract announcement: https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-awards-company-to-attempt-swift-spacecraft-orbit-boost/

Footage: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center and Wallops Flight Facility via the Scientific Visualization Studio: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/15051 (with Katalyst Space and Northrop Grumman), https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/15044 , https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/15060 , https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/15061 , https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/10170 , https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/14721 . Public domain; NASA does not endorse this video. Spacecraft-in-orbit shots are animations (labelled on screen). The Pegasus air-launch shot is an earlier launch, not the July 2026 flight. Swift launch footage: November 2004. Charts and maps: NEXORA.
Narration: synthetic voice (ElevenLabs).
